about.title: San Juan Capistrano Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: San Juan Capistrano draws locals and visitors alike to its historic Mission, downtown shops, and businesses along Del Obispo Street and Camino Capistrano. When a property owner lets a spill, broken pavement, or poor lighting go unaddressed, an ordinary walk can end in a serious fall. California law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn visitors — which is why documenting the scene and pulling surveillance footage quickly matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or negotiate settlements; we're a free connection service. If you were injured in a fall on someone else's property in San Juan Capistrano, we can put you in touch with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Reach out and describe what happened so we can start the process of finding the right fit for your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Your Claim

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, inspection records, and witness statements to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses along Camino Capistrano and Del Obispo Street overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Bar, Recovery
items.desc: Even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to still pursue compensation for the share of fault attributed to the property owner.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in San Juan Capistrano?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city facility, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's wise to speak with an attorney soon after the fall so deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: What if I fell at a business near the Mission or downtown shops?
items.answer: Commercial property owners in areas like downtown San Juan Capistrano are expected to maintain safe walkways for visitors, including keeping floors clear and walkways free of hazards. If a hazard existed long enough that the owner should have noticed it, that can support a premises liability claim. Photos of the hazard and any nearby surveillance cameras can help document what happened.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service and does not charge you to find an independent attorney. Attorneys in our network typically work on a contingency basis, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. LawProactive itself is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice.
